Interface feedback in the 150 to 250ms range feels immediate. Longer than about 400ms starts to feel like waiting.
Use 150-250ms for hovers and toggles, up to 400ms for large panel moves.
Things entering the screen should decelerate; things leaving should accelerate. Linear motion feels mechanical.
Use ease-out for entering, ease-in for leaving, ease-in-out for moves.
Animating width, top or margin forces layout every frame. Transform and opacity stay on the compositor.
Animate transform and opacity; avoid layout properties.
transition:all animates things you did not intend, such as layout changes on resize, and costs more.
List only the properties that should move.
Animation that does not explain a change, such as a hero that drifts for no reason, is decoration and tires the eye.
Animate to show cause and effect, orientation or state; remove anything that explains nothing.
Add movement to every element for polish.
Infinite pulses, spinners that never resolve and bouncing arrows pull attention from the task and burn battery.
Run loops only while loading or live, stop them afterwards.
Pulse a fake 'live' dot or a bouncing chevron forever.
Sections that fade up on scroll the same way every time slow reading and flag a template. Use reveals where order matters.
Reveal only elements whose entrance explains something; keep content visible without script.
Fade and slide every section on enter.
Layers moving at different speeds can cause motion sickness and cost scroll performance.
Use subtle parallax on one element and disable under reduced motion.
Apply it to the whole page.
The View Transitions API smooths changes between states or pages without hand-rolled clones.
Wrap state updates in document.startViewTransition where supported, with a plain fallback.
If a user clicks again mid-animation and the UI waits, it feels laggy or lands in the wrong state.
Use CSS transitions that reverse smoothly, or cancel running animations.
Block input until the animation ends.
Flashing a spinner for 100ms feels worse than none. Show it only after a short delay and keep it up for a minimum time.
Wait about 200ms before showing a spinner.
will-change reserves memory for each element. Applied broadly it slows pages down.
Apply it shortly before an animation and remove after.
A 4000px photo in a 400px slot wastes bandwidth. srcset and sizes let the browser pick.
Provide srcset with widths and a sizes hint; use AVIF or WebP.
loading='lazy' saves data for images that may never be seen, but delays ones in the first view.
Lazy-load images below the first screen; never the main one.
Largest Contentful Paint measures when the main image or heading appears. fetchpriority and preloading speed it up.
Add fetchpriority='high' to the hero image and preload its font.
Wait for JavaScript to inject the hero.
Web fonts block text rendering unless told otherwise. font-display:swap shows a fallback immediately.
Use font-display:swap or optional, preload the main face and subset the file.
Each weight and style is another file. Two or three is usually enough for a site.
Load only weights used and prefer a variable font.
Load every weight of a family.
Chat widgets, tag managers and trackers add weight and block interaction. Each one needs a reason.
Load third-party code after interaction or idle and remove unused tags.
Add every vendor's snippet in the head.
Scripts that block parsing delay first paint. defer and type=module run after the HTML is parsed.
Use defer or module for scripts and split large bundles by route.
Put large scripts in the head without defer.
Hashed filenames can be cached for a year, so repeat visits cost nothing.
Send Cache-Control with immutable and a long max-age on hashed assets.
Serve assets with no cache headers.
Interaction to Next Paint tracks how soon the page reacts to taps and keys. Long tasks on the main thread cause lag.
Break up long JavaScript tasks and move heavy work off the main thread.
Run big loops inside click handlers.
Background video can weigh tens of megabytes. A poster image and compressed formats load faster.
Set preload='none' with a poster and offer reasonable bitrates.
Reading layout (offsetHeight) then writing styles in a loop forces repeated reflow.
Autoplaying video burns data and battery and distracts. Let visitors start it.
Show a poster and a play button; honour prefers-reduced-data where possible.
A page weight target, such as under 1 MB for a brochure site, forces choices that help every visitor on a slow connection.
Set a budget per page and check it in the build.
